title: Permutation in String
statement:
Given two strings `s1` and `s2`, return `true` if `s2` contains a permutation of `s1`, or `false` otherwise.

In other words, return `true` if one of `s1`'s permutations is a substring of `s2`.

Since a permutation just rearranges characters, this is equivalent to sliding a fixed-size window of length `s1.length` across `s2` and checking whether the window's character counts exactly match `s1`'s character counts.
constraints: s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: s2 contains one permutation of s1 ("ba").

editorial.approach: If `s1.length > s2.length`, return false immediately. Otherwise build a frequency count of `s1`, then slide a window of size `s1.length` across `s2`, maintaining a running frequency count for the current window. After each slide (add the new right character, remove the character leaving on the left), compare the window's frequency count to `s1`'s. If they ever match exactly, return true. Comparing counts can be done in O(26) using a fixed-size array instead of a full map-equality check, keeping the whole scan O(n).
